implementation_notes: JPA maps a many-to-many onto an intermediate table: a Collection (usually Set) on each entity, @ManyToMany on the owning side plus @JoinTable naming the table and the two foreign-key columns (or defaults derived from the attribute names), and mappedBy on the inverse side. The provider inserts and deletes rows in the join table as the collection changes, which is Association Table Mapping with the table hidden from the model. Use it while the association has no payload; the join table is created by the schema generator, and the composite key over the two foreign keys is what keeps links unique.
pitfalls: Only the owning side writes the join table; adding to the inverse collection is silently ignored unless the owning side is updated too.
Lombok-generated equals/hashCode/toString over the collection recurses across both entities, and fetching it outside the persistence context throws LazyInitializationException.

A List (rather than Set) without @OrderColumn is treated as an unordered bag: the provider may delete and re-insert the whole collection's link rows on every change, and duplicates appear in the join table.
CascadeType.REMOVE on a many-to-many deletes the associated entities, not just the links - it is almost never what the association means.
The default join table and column names are derived from the attribute names, so a renamed field silently renames the schema unless @JoinTable is explicit.

variants.name: Association entity mapped over the join table
variants.implementation_notes: When the link carries data or must be queried in its own right, the join table is mapped as an entity: an @Entity with a composite key (an @EmbeddedId id class, or a surrogate id protected by a unique constraint over the pair) and two @ManyToOne associations, while the ends keep collections of the association entity instead of each other. This is the documented promotion of the pattern into an association entity, and it trades the convenience of the direct collection for the ability to attach attributes, audit the link, and query it with JPQL.
pitfalls: The composite key is immutable: re-pointing a link means deleting the row, not updating a column.
Without @MapsId (or with a plain surrogate key) nothing stops the same actor-film pair from being inserted twice unless a unique constraint is declared explicitly.
Both @ManyToOne associations are eager by default in the id-class style if not marked lazy, so loading one link pulls both ends.
variants.idiom_name: Association entity mapped over the join table
